reasons.specificity: The ledger accurately reconstructs the distinct roles of Benjamin, Tenbruck, Simmel, Marx, Schumpeter, civilizational theory, and paradigm/myth research in Deutschmann’s argument.
reasons.anchoring: All quoted anchors occur in the article and generally warrant the attributed moves, mechanisms, qualifications, and limits.
reasons.non_obviousness: It usefully isolates the negative tertium comparationis, selective Marx–Schumpeter compatibility, institutionalization’s profitability trade-off, and the difference between timeless religious and cyclical capitalist myths.
reasons.coherence: The substantive reconstruction is consistent, but the final scope assessment calls every dimension “inconclusive” because of malformed metadata after repeatedly declaring complete inspection and supported findings.
reasons.usefulness: The construction ledger and theory–evidence table directly serve the requested reading task and clearly distinguish claimed synthesis from demonstrated conceptual work.
reasons.hallucination_risk: Unsupported invention is minimal, though labels such as “middle-range” and “structural analogy” are interpretive rather than Deutschmann’s own, and the malformed CHECK/scope apparatus creates avoidable uncertainty.

decisive_errors.analysis_claim: The inventory repeatedly reports findings as “supported within the stated scope” after “complete reported inspection,” but the Scope assessment declares the same six dimensions “inconclusive; not supported by a completed scope review.”
decisive_errors.counter_passage: The supplied article is complete from Abstract through sections I–IV, and the analysis itself supplies direct anchors from all relevant sections; the later inconclusive verdict results from a metadata-validation error rather than contrary or missing source evidence.

score.one_line: An exceptionally well-anchored, source-specific construction ledger whose main defect is an internally contradictory and extraneous scope-validation appendix.
